utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So before May, there were no restrictions on the freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were no restrictions, but there was heightened control, ever since the beginning of the second half of 1991. That is control by the police on the roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Communications within Kljuc, were you still able, before May, to receive broadcasts from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as broadcasts are concerned, sometime in April, we were no longer able to receive Sarajevo, as far as the media were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how was that prevented?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This was prevented in such a way that the relay station at Kozara was redirected towards Belgrade, so only programmes from Belgrade and Banja Luka could be viewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, again, before the 7th of May, did you ever see any weaponry in the area of Kljuc town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As regards weaponry, the town of Kljuc was full of weapons, with respect to the groups I mentioned, those that were going as volunteers to the front. And then also when the Knin Corps appeared at Laniste.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever see artillery at all, as opposed to personal weaponry?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did see some at Laniste, when we made a joint visit there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what struck you about the artillery you saw at Laniste?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I saw guns turned towards Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before the 7th of May, had there been any dismissals of Bosniaks from their jobs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were dismissals. The first started in the neighbouring municipality of Drvar. I know this because a group of employees came to the municipality, people who had worked at the Sipad plant in Drvar and they had been dismissed in April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the reason given for their dismissal?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They told us that they were dismissed merely because they were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than that, in that group in Sipad, the Sipad plant, sorry, were there any dismissals that had taken place of Bosniaks within Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Already in April and the beginning of May, the executive -- people were dismissed from executive positions so that the first to be dismissed was the editor-in-chief of the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before the 7th of May, had you, the Muslim population in Kljuc, done anything to try and arm yourselves?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Before the 7th of May, I think there were attempts by individuals to procure weapons because of the security situation, which was in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you yourself possess a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I personally had a pistol, with a licence, a legal licence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you say that there were attempts by individuals to procure weapons, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The very closeness of the front in Croatia and the opening of a front at Kupres and especially the return of combatants from those fronts instilled fear and jeopardised the security, and people fearing this, armed themselves by purchasing weapons from certain people who came to the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any attempt, first, by yourself personally, to buy weapons on a large scale?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In those days, one could not even think of it, since there was complete control over all the roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So -- I'm sorry, is the answer to my question, then, no, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the second question is, appreciating your answer but were you aware of anyone else attempting to buy weapons on a large scale?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that on the 7th of May, there was this, as it were, takeover. You say Serbian flags appeared and the police force's insignia changed. Were there other signs of things happening?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as the composition of the police force was concerned, it was virtually of one ethnicity and the same applied to the bodies of Kljuc municipality, in which only Serbs were employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that there weren't proper or there weren't many restrictions before the 7th of May on the freedom of movement. What happened after the 7th of May?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of May, checkpoints were set up with barbed wire and there was control of every vehicle at each of those checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you become aware, first of all, of the establishment of a Crisis Staff in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When did you first hear about a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard of it for the first time at the end of 1991 or the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who did you hear -- from whom did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This was no secret in Kljuc. I heard it from many people, including Mr. Banjac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Banjac or other people explain to you why there was a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you, the Bosniaks, form any kind of a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At what stage?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There was an attempt to form such a staff in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was the head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In the -- at first, it should have been Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Which one? Which one of the Filipovics?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just a clarification, Your Honour, he says there was an attempt to form a Crisis Staff in mid-May. Of what year is he referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's have the two questions. So mid-May of which year, 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And you said that when -- to the question as to who was the head of this Crisis Staff, that the Bosniaks set up, you said at first it should have been Mr. Filipovic. My question to you is: Which one of the Filipovics because we have heard at least about three of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muhamed Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Muhamed Filipovic the professor or Muhamed Filipovic, Omer's brother, son of Suljo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The brother, Omer's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Actually four Filipovics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you say there was an attempt to form the Crisis Staff. Why wasn't it successful, it was only an attempt?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was an attempt because from the 7th of May, movement was already restricted and we were not able to meet. We didn't have any conditions to be able to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about a TO staff? Was there an attempt to set up a TO staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was formed after the appointment of the commander of the TO staff by the commander of the TO staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And firstly, who was appointed the commander?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Omer Filipovic was appointed the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that, you say, was by the commander of the TO staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Once it had been formed, were you able to organise units?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We couldn't organise them because we were already in such a situation that it was impossible to move around on the ground, since checkpoints were already set up and the staff was considered to be illegal, even though it was the legal staff of the Territorial Defence for the municipality of Kljuc, within the TO staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the third Crisis Staff I want to ask you about is this: Did you hear about a Crisis Staff in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when did you first hear of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard about it for the first time sometime in April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just another clarification, I think the evidence so far has established that there were three Crisis Staffs in Banja Luka and I just like to know which one the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There were three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was -- the question was Crisis Staff in Banja Luka. So let's leave it at that for the time being and if there are any further questions on it, I mean, the witness was being asked specifically now on which Crisis Staff he had come to know about in April. I know what you mean and actually it was in my mind but I think I would rather not interfere at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask some further questions, had Mr. Ackerman weighted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would have expected you to, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you've heard about a Crisis Staff in Banja Luka sometime in April. Do you know who the head of that Crisis Staff was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard that it was Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any connections before your arrest at the end of May, between that Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, headed by Mr. Brdjanin, and the Crisis Staff in Kljuc, the SDS Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything in particular. From the document which I received by accident -- except from the document which I received by accident.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. There was a translation problem there. All right. Now, after the takeover in -- on the 7th of May, were there any further -- were there any dismissals that you became aware of?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: All the Bosniak executive officials were dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And by that, the executive officials on the executive council of the municipality? Or do you mean executive positions elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: All posts in the municipality held by Bosniaks, especially those from companies, first of all the management was dismissed and then the employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you owned a pistol with a licence for it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember hearing any announcement on the radio or on television or elsewhere about weapons having to be surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard this announcement on Radio Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was being ordered to surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The announcement applied to Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you surrender your weapon?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't surrender it right away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Just like the majority of the citizens, I didn't do it because I was concerned about my safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was -- when they -- when the surrender was made on the radio, was anything said about what would happen if weapons weren't surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: A deadline was set, as far as I can recall, the deadline was the 15th of May, until midnight. If weapons were not handed over, the strictest measures would be applied against those who still possessed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you did hand over your weapon?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I handed over my weapon on the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to come, then, please, to your arrest. I think it's right that you were arrested on the 28th of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before your arrest, had you become aware of other events?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I found out that some citizens had been arrested before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any fighting that had started?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: On the 27th, I heard that there was an incident in the area of Pudin Han in Busija.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what had you heard had happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard that after the a announcement to hand over weapons was made, the police and the army went to disarm Bosniaks in the neighbourhoods where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you yourself try and go to any of these areas?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I personally did not, because I was in a wood with my family, since the entire population had already left their homes because of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us, then, please, how were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of May, I wounded myself from the pistol that I owned and then I went to the hospital. At the first checkpoint, I was arrested and taken to the Stara Gradiska prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can I just -- sorry. Was this another pistol from the one you'd surrendered? Or are we still talking about the same pistol?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: With my own pistol, after this happened, this pistol stayed in the place where this happened, so that the people who were there handed it over.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You had your pistol for which you had a licence.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think you told us you handed over your weapon on the 27th of May. So the day before your arrest.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. On the 28th, after I injured myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you only -- did you ever have more than the one pistol?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just the one. All right. You say you wounded yourself in the foot. You then went to hospital or tried to go to hospital but you were stopped at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's at that stage that the pistol was taken from you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. Not then. Because I didn't have the pistol with me. I left the pistol in the house where I was sleeping, at the place where I had inflicted the wound on myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So was it you personally who handed over the pistol to the authorities or did somebody else do it on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't do it personally. Omer Filipovic handed it over.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to the checkpoint, you say you were arrested. Did -- firstly, who was at the checkpoint, military or police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was the reserves of the Serbian police, they manned the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The people who or the person who arrested you, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I knew some of them, just by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They didn't say anything. They just escorted me to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what happened to you at the police station?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: At the police station, they said that I should wait for a while and after that, they put me into an ambulance and took me to the Stara Gradiska prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you before you got to Stara Gradiska prison?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They beat me in Kljuc. That was the first thing. And then in Banja Luka, at the place where the Mali Logor barracks is, they beat me again, with another 20 men who were in trailer-truck, who were also being sent to the Stara Gradiska prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we take this, please in stages? You say you were beaten in Kljuc. Was that immediately when you got to the police station or later on?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Immediately when I got to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you had the injury to your foot treated before then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who beat you? Did you know the people or the person who beat you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know one of them. His name is Boro Ceko.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how many of them were involved in this beating?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: About four or five persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where did the beating take place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: On the steps at the very entrance to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What were they using to beat you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They used batons, rifle butts, their feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did they say anything whilst they were carrying out this beating?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't remember what they said because I was semi-conscious.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't remember the -- I'm sorry, I don't expect you to remember the exact words but can you give us a general idea of the sort of things that were being said before you became semi-conscious?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Mostly they cursed me, they used curses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did they know who you were?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What injuries did you suffer as a result of that first beating?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: My lower jaw was broken and some of my ribs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was outside the police station. Were there any beatings inside the police station before you were transferred?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Not at the police station, because I wasn't there for a very long time. They said I was going back, and then on the way out of the police station, the same people who were on the steps beat me again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think 59 line 20, where it says, "lower jaw," I believe what he said was his lower lip, not his lower jaw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it -- but was it your lower lip or your lower jaw, the jaw is this, the lip is this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This whole part, around my lips, it was all cut and I still have the scars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But did you have a fracture of the bone of the jaw, of this bone here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not the bone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Mr. Ackerman? Thank you. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. They beat you again when you came out of the police station. Was it at that stage that you were put into the ambulance?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, when they beat me, then I was taken to the hospital in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And which hospital were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There is one hospital in Kljuc, and they took me to that hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you receive treatment, first of all, for the injury to your foot?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. They dressed my wound and I received anti-poisoning serum.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the injuries to your face that you described, or your ribs? Were those dealt with?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They didn't really treat that, and on top of everything, I was beaten some more by the guards in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that before you went in for the treatment to your foot or after?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Before my foot was dressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Once your foot had been dressed, where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Then they took me back in the ambulance to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you remain at the police station for any length of time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. I waited there for a while, and then the ambulance started to follow a trailer-truck, which was covered by tarpaulin, in the direction of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And once in Banja Luka, were you taken directly to Mali Logor, the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We arrived at Banja Luka in the evening, and we were in front of the barracks, we were not taken inside the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've said that you were beaten at Mali Logor. Was that inside the barracks or outside?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In front of the barracks on the road leading to Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who carried out the beating on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The driver and the police officer, they went into the barracks and then four policemen came out who beat me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the beatings were all carried out by policemen, were they?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not completely sure. They all wore uniforms. They were all uniformed persons, so I don't know whether they were from the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you couldn't distinguish the army uniforms from the police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's 12.30, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to finish this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, when these -- the second, or this beating took place, were weapons used or was it just hands and feet?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They used their fists, batons, they kicked me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you suffer any further injuries as a result of that beating?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I received injuries to my head. I had bleeding from my head, from my mouth and from my nose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From there, were you taken direct to Stara Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's where I saw for the first time that the trailer-truck which was driving in front of us also had people inside, and these people were also beaten. After they were put into the trailer-truck again, we went to the Stara Gradiska prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, that will be a convenient moment. Your Honour we've got the original of that document Mr. Ackerman queried about and all the underlining was on the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Ms. Korner. 20 minutes? Would it be okay, 20 minutes? Okay. 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, before Your Honours leave we better discuss the timing at the end of today's session, I think we are all now in complete confusion about what's happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't be able to complete in time -- I think Your Honour has just seen the medical certificate. My examination of Mr. Egrlic today, although the bulk of it. So I wonder if we could stop at 1.30 just so we can try and sort out once and for all what's happening. 1.30 for Mr. Egrlic, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you told us that you were then taken to Stara Gradiska. How long did you remain in Stara Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I stayed there about 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And from there, were you transferred to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Manjaca, were your injuries any worse than they were when you arrived at Stara Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as my wound is concerned, it was treated up to a point, and the other injuries were recovering of their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at any stage before your arrival at Manjaca, were you interrogated -- were you interrogated? Questioned?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where were you questioned?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They started questioning me in Stara Gradiska and then they continued at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And the questioning was done by whom at Stara Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In Stara Gradiska, and in Manjaca, by a captain. I just know his nickname, Cila [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, could you say the nickname again? The interpreter didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Zenga was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that a police captain or a military captain?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Military, a captain in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to deal, then, please, with Manjaca. Were you arrived -- sorry, when you arrived, was the camp already set up and operating?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were there already prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were, men from Grapska. I think it was the Doboj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you were taken there, were you on your own or with a number of other people?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was in a large group of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were they all from Kljuc or were they were other areas as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That group was mostly from Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you got to Manjaca, were you placed into one of the stables?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were the men with whom you arrived place into the same stables -- stable?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were there already people in that stable?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to deal first of all then with the interrogations. This man, this Captain Zenga, what was he asking you about?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This captain asked me, in particular, about the events that took place in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In Manjaca, when you were being interrogated by him, was anything happening to you during those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Before each interrogation and after the interrogation, they would beat me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who would beat you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The police who were guarding the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The man interrogating you was military. Were there other military in the room with you or was it police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The policemen would usually be in front of the door and he would be inside with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you were interrogated, how did you feel?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I felt terrible. He threatened me. It was a question of my life being on the line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see any notes being taken at the time of the questioning?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Notes were taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to you look first of all, please, at a document that is headed "Official note." It's dated the 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I'm not sure whether Your Honours have got this. Can I hand to Your Honours a bundle of documents? There is one for the registry. I think if Your Honours go to the second document in there, with the number 0 -- which is the translation. Yes. 03039888. It's headed "Official note" dated the 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want you -- I think you've had a chance to look at this before, but before you were shown this, did you ever see this at the time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we need to go through, then, what it is alleged you said. It's an official note compiled on the 17th of June, 1992, about an interview with you and it gives your background or rather your jobs, and it says, "Regarding the armed revolt and the circumstances surrounding the organisation of an ambush on the police and attack on a military convoy." Let's deal with this sentence by sentence, please. He stated that "the formation of the municipal staff of the so-called Bosanski Kljuc TO came through the republican BH TO staff. And the same facts appointed Omer Filipovic commander of the Bosanski Kljuc TO." Can we stop there? Was that something you told this Captain Zenga?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then you stated that "the President of the Kljuc assembly was also aware of the formation of the Bosanski Kljuc TO." And that "the Bosanski Kljuc TO was formed because they expected that the Kljuc municipality would be divided on the territorial principle into Bosanski Kljuc and Kljuc municipality if there were political discussions." Did you say that to the captain?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then "the talks, discussions, and meetings were held in the party offices in the Kljuc cultural centre and in the small meeting hall of Kljuc Municipal Assembly" -- of the Kljuc assembly, rather, I should say. Was that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "The condition of authorised officials of the Kljuc SJB, having to sign a declaration of loyalty contributed to the speed with which the TO of the so-called Bosanski Kljuc was formed." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "Those employed in the Kljuc TO and those from the Kljuc SJB who did not sign the declaration of loyalty to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were supposed it to join the staff command." Did you say that to the captain?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next to -- well, I'm sorry, you didn't say it. Was that true? Was that actually what happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. This didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say you emphasised that you personally "did not talk to these people but assumed that they would probably have consented in order to secure the subsistence of their families since they had no jobs." Did you say something like that to the interrogator?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again, I have to ask you, was it true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then it goes on, "When asked who replaced Suad Mesic as the person responsible for medical matters in the Bosanski Kljuc TO staff, you replied that it was most likely to be Dr. Emir Kapetanovic." Were you asked questions about the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So did you say this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then it goes on, "after reporting to the republican BH TO Staff on the 28th of April, 1992, that the municipal TO staff of Kljuc municipality had not declared its loyalty to the republican staff, they started to form the Bosanski Kljuc staff." It's very unclear who is supposed to be -- whether this is the interrogate -- the report, or you. Was there any questions about this type of subject matter?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They are always talking about Bosanski Kljuc. It wasn't the Bosanski Kljuc staff that was being formed here but the TO staff of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps we can go on to the next sentence. "We found the grounds for the --" yes, I think this must be the interrogator. "The founding of the Bosanski Kljuc TO staff in a decision adopted in the Kljuc assembly which provided for the mounting of a village guard in all local communes in Kljuc municipality." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It wasn't in our jurisdiction to seek a base. The staff was formed on the basis of a decision from the TO staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that but can you tell us, what it's talking about here is that a village guard was mounted in local communes. First of all, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were village guards and all of those who worked in the common bodies of the municipality knew about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you -- were you asked about this by your interrogator, Captain Zenga?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then it goes on to list the people who were members of the Crisis Staff. First, is that an accurate list?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've already stated this -- as far as the Crisis Staff is concerned, it never started functioning because we formed or tried to form, at the time, when it was already difficult to move around, there were restrictions on movement, so this staff wasn't able to meet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I understand that but when it was decided to form it, were those including yourself, those people, supposed to be members?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. The Crisis Staff was supposed to comprise the legally elected bodies of the Bosniaks who participated in the joint bodies of the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But would that have included you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I was the president of the executive board. That was my function.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then it goes on to talk, it at the bottom, to say this, "Since the Bosnia-Herzegovina Territorial Defence required that the commander of the Bosanski Kljuc Territorial Defence have a university education, the following were appointed commanders of Bosanski Kljuc Territorial Defence," Filipovic, Amir Abdic, Nevzad Djeric, and yourself. Now, is that right, were you yourself appointed a commander by directive from the Bosnia-Herzegovina Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's not true. Only Mr. Omer Filipovic was appointed commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it goes on to say about you, "We have established through operative information that he was also responsible for arming." Was that true? Were you made responsible for collecting arms?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is not true. I was in charge of policy and of carrying out political activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next sentence relates to you and says that you told them, your interrogators, that the village guards grew into platoons and companies. Did you say that to your interrogators?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that. This -- they stayed at the level of guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then they said you were asked how soldiers in the Kljuc -- the Bosanski Kljuc TO were armed and you said that this was achieved through individual purchases of weapons. First, did you say that to the captain?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's true. It's possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then it goes on, "However, there was also help from abroad, mostly they relied on people from our area employed in Switzerland who, under the pretense of collecting humanitarian aid, in fact collected money for weapons and ammunition." Did you say that to the interrogators?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I said that as far as the diaspora is concerned, the money was collected mostly for humanitarian purposes. This is something that was added on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then it says that you and another man named Bilic had gone to Zagreb for a meeting with the people from Switzerland and that you collected 18.000 Swiss francs and returned home and for sometime the money was in your house until you took it to Sarajevo. First of all, did you in fact collect 18.000 Swiss francs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's true that we went to Zagreb and that we were given funds to provide humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you in fact take it, to Sarajevo, to the SDA offices?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that later on, weapons were driven to Kljuc in a white Golf with Sarajevo registration plates. Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you yourself say anything like this, Mr. Egrlic, to the interrogators, on the basis that by that stage you'd been beaten?.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I said that weapons were procured through contacts with people within the broader area of the municipality, but that there was no organised procurement of weapons in large quantities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So all of this part that suggests that you had bought and later, as we can see, lists of weapons you're alleged to have had, is any of that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. There is no truth in it, because people got weapons individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It suggests that you actually acquired a Slovenian submachine-gun, which you left behind after you'd been wounded, and buried. Did you own a Slovenian submachine-gun?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I only owned a pistol legally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it suggests that you gave a Croatian submachine-gun, a Zagi, to Omer Filipovic and your brother and Ibrahim Egrlic. Did you give them these weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then according to them, you were asked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Please, what's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to call the attention of the transcript folks to page 72, line 3. It's clearly something wrong there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I appreciate -- I think when it's serious but this will be picked up Your Honour, quite honestly, something like that, when we go through. There is a difference between a mistake in the translation and what's typed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, please, no interruptions unless absolutely necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now that I've lost my place, yes, at the bottom -- you why asked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was the whole idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was indeed, Your Honour. That's why I'm objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was not the whole idea. Usually there is a little caret when they say they are going to make a correction. I'm not satisfied that they would pick that up and it's incorrect and I wasn't trying to interrupt Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman, for clearing that up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You were asked, according to this note, where you were, Mr. Egrlic, prior to the shooting, prior to the incident, clearly, in Pudin Han or wherever and you said on the 26th of May you attended a meeting at the cultural centre in Pudin Han. First of all, were you asked where you'd been?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you tell them, as is recorded here, that you attended a meeting in Pudin Han?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And apparently you said that the meeting was attended by company and platoon commanders. Did you say something like that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. These people who are mentioned here were present and they are members of the executive board of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the meeting about?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The meeting was about the problems that arose with respect to the security situation in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then it talks about the convoy being attacked at Krasulje, that you spent the night in Pudin Han, and describes how you received your injury with the pistol. Did you tell the interrogators about this? I mean is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I told them that I spent the night at Pudin Han because my family had moved out, as had the entire area I lived in, because of the shooting there was there so that I spent the night at Pudin Han in a house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But then describes -- it apparently states how you received the injury. Is that an accurate description of how you received your injury to the foot?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it then states that after going to hospital in Kljuc, you were taken by ambulance to the Banja Luka health centre. Did you ever go to the Banja Luka Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I was taken to the prison in Stara Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever say to your interrogators that you had been taken to the Banja Luka Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then there is something about a fax machine in Pudin Han cultural centre. Did you ever speak to the interrogators about a fax machine?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. A telefax was to have been connected that day and that is why I was there, for the connection of the telefax and roughly what is stated here is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think you've said you hadn't seen this document before you were shown it by us, but were you shown any sort of note that had been made by the interrogators at the time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As regards the note on the interrogation, some notes were done in such a way that the official person wrote them and others I personally wrote because I was forced to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to show you -- and I think now -- not tomorrow, Monday, the one that you wrote yourself personally. Your Honour, regrettably I forgot to put in the list. It's one of the ones I noticed this morning. I was doing it at such a speed yesterday but I will have copies available for Your Honours tomorrow -- Monday. Your Honour could that document that he's just read through become Prosecutor's Exhibit 1113? 1113?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's all for today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour because I want to try and finally sort out the question of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Egrlic, we have to stop here for today because we have got other matters to discuss. You will be brought back to this courtroom on Monday and we will take it up from there. Thank you. You will now be escorted by the usher. If during the weekend, between now and Monday, you need anything, I suppose you have been give and contact point and I'm sure you will be attended to as necessary. Incidentally, give him back the ear phones, please. Because I don't know, are there any other witnesses here in The Hague? I suppose so. May I also remind you that between now and Monday, you're not to discuss any of the matters you are giving evidence upon with anyone? That's very important. I have your word? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour can I just -- Ms. Gustin has kindly reminded me that in fact you probably have this already. Can I just confirm that because you were given a bundle of all the statements that he'd made. This is one headed "Military secret" and it's 03039891. It's not in the bundle you got this morning but at an earlier stage. And it's Manjaca prisoner of war camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, can I then try -- Mr. Ackerman and I did talk in the break about this and I'm not sure -- I think we have all been at slightly cross-purposes. But can I first of all say to Your Honour that I will be about another hour on Monday morning with Mr. Egrlic, more or less completed just a few documents that are in that. I don't know how long Mr. Ackerman is going to be in cross-examination with him but the next witness, 7.196, we estimate will be in chief at the moment, unfortunately the lawyer who is calling him is not available but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just drawing the attention of my assistant because that's -- because I'm mentioning this very, very simply because the other witness that we discussed this morning, the one to whom the certificate refers to is actually a follow-up or --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was a Rule 92 witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes exactly but it's being put -- this witness has been described as having evidence which is cumulative to that given by 7.196 and I was going to draw your attention that 7.196 hasn't been brought forward as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's coming on Monday. He's the one that kept being put back when we had all the trouble with Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's estimated to last - although I think it may be less from my conversation was Mr. Nicholls but five hours but it may be less. Because a lot of, I think, a lot of what he would have covered has been covered by Mr. Filipovic already. 7.119, two hours. And the last two are, that is 7.101 and 7.191, they are both 30 minutes cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 30 minutes cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They are both -- Your Honours ordered that they were to come, the Rule 92 witnesses and they were to have 30 minutes cross-examination. So, Your Honour, that, by my guess, means we wrap it up on Wednesday, give or take, depending on obviously how long Mr. Egrlic is going to last and how long 7.196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I have no reason to quarrel with those estimates. That's -- it may be a little longer than Ms. Korner thinks but that's probably pretty close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will probably try to make an exception to the rule and I'll try to intervene and try and restrict it further if necessary. So I will make sure that I will read thoroughly their statements before they give evidence, to make sure then to restrict the evidence to what is basically really necessary. And I will be asking for your cooperation of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in fact I won't be calling any of these witnesses but as I say 7.196 I seem to recall Mr. Nicholls telling me before he left because a lot of it had been covered by Filipovic, he thought it would be reduced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will it be even better.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, so that's that. Your Honour, my application will be that in the light of Mr. -- the witness's medical history, and the fact that he's cumulative to 7.196, that his statement be entered notwithstanding the Defence objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what -- whether Mr. Ackerman has had time to go through the details. I haven't. I've asked the legal officer to feed me on that, because as it is, I don't remember, and you don't expect me to remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On what basis General Talic had asked for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can remind you of that, Your Honour I've got the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have not got a clue and I don't remember the contents of the statement of the witness, so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he deals -- let me just find the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if we can't deal with this on Monday so we will all have a chance to be aware of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was about to say, that's going to be my application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And there is also because, as I see it, this medical certificate, there are some words that I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it's been translated, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't think it has been completely translated for example the last line it's subdicom [phoen] in the original language, with my limited knowledge of the subject, I don't know what it means. And the same as far as kemicom [phoen] I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I say, and we have had a discussion with him and I can call the investigator if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see that is that says, "Ischaemic heart." All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's got heart trouble and he can't travel. That's the effects of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The certificate doesn't say so. Normally I would require a certificate not only to tell us what he's suffering from but also whether he's in a condition to travel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm afraid Your Honour we had a sort of last minute -- but as I say if necessary I can call evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What I suggest in any case is this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I should add he's 67 and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Anyhow, Your Honour, that's our application. Your Honour can deal with it on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime I would have had a chance to read the relevant part of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I need to confirm, Mr. Ackerman is absolutely right, this heart condition was entered on to records. It was just missed when -- so it's not something we suddenly discovered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm just hoping Ms. Korner is not suggesting 67 and a half makes you too old to travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope not. It gets you near to the age when the insurance will not cover you any more but.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was the combination of age and medical condition, Your Honour, I was trying to refer to. Your Honour, can we now finally try to sort out when we are sitting? Mr. Ackerman -- we tried to sort out all this confusion. Mr. Ackerman's view is that if he has the next three days, that the three days, the 21st off, then he doesn't object to having the extra three days replaced at the end of November. So we are in the position now, as I understand it, whereby if you agree to it, we would be sitting the 20th, 21st, and 22nd of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The idea would be precisely that. Originally it was planned not to sit on those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My suggestion was -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour can I just say, if Mr. Ackerman -- Can I understand this? If Mr. Ackerman is given, let us say the best part of all of -- from Wednesday of next week unexpectedly, then I'm not sure whether or not that would satisfy his need before we start on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we stop on Wednesday, the 16th, then there is Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then as you say we would only be sitting three days that week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we would be sitting only three days and then you would have four days the week after. Perhaps you would be -- you would do what I personally at least plan to do, and that -- take it not all in one bulk but to take it -- I know that you as Defence counsel have got different roles than we have, because you have to prepare cross-examination and ask questions based supposedly on the totality of the evidence or of the documentation. Problem that there is obviously is a logistical one apart from what Mr. Ackerman has rightly pointed out, and that is we can't leave it until the -- until it is too late in the day for the Prosecution to know whether they ought to bring forward a witness or not. I mean also because of the problems that there is -- that there are of bringing forward witnesses and also the desire not to -- the desire to economise on the resources of the Tribunal in any case. So I don't know, I mean, we are quite open. Do you think that if we stop on Wednesday, and we all make a true and full effort to finish next week's work by the end of Wednesday evening, then perhaps if you have those four days, 17, 18, 19, and 20th, we could at least try and start on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had a conversation with Ms. Korner near the end of the session or maybe at the end of the session yesterday and was informed that she thought she would be finished on Wednesday or Thursday, so I already knew that. And I had that in mind when I made my application to you today that I would have those days, plus. So that's not something we just discovered after I had made my remarks to you this morning. The -- part of the problem is that I absolutely must leave the country to interview a witness which I was planning to do this weekend. That seems to have fallen through. That means I'll probably have to do it at the ends of next week which does free me up to work on some things but I've got to work on what's coming up next week. So I just don't know how to find the time. I am perfectly willing to make every effort that I can to accommodate this Trial Chamber. I really am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm convinced of that, Mr. Ackerman, otherwise I would not even be addressing you. Would it be too late for you, Ms. Korner, if we take a decision on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It would be too late.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm afraid it would because the VWS require to know on Monday who we are bringing up on Friday, if not this Friday, and we've already told Mr. Sejmenovic that he will be required for Monday, the 21st. He's in a position where he finds this all quite nerve-wracking, so if we are not going to call him, he needs to be informed straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He can always be informed on Monday, if we come to the conclusion that we are not starting -- sitting on the 21st. The office, victims and witnesses, can be informed that the intention of the Tribunal is to sit on the 21st but then if are -- we decide otherwise on the 14th, they will just be informed, as they have been informed in the past, that the witness will not be forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour it really would assist for a number of reasons, we also have to -- as I said we have to reorganise, if Your Honour is going to give the 21st off, we have to reorganise the order. So I think a decision, if Your Honours don't mind, must be taken today, if you notify us verbally later today or through your staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Things being what they have been described to us and there being no reason to doubt in the least that the amount of documents that have been -- that have to be looked into by the Defence in preparation for its work, particularly in cross-examining the first of these witnesses. How long do you intend to examine in chief, Sejmenovic? Because I would understand that there will be a statement already, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is -- he's testified once, twice, Tadic, Keraterm, three times before, plus the statement that was taken specifically to deal with his knowledge of Mr. Brdjanin about which he hasn't testified yet. But I mean, Your Honours you will see that on the last time that he went -- Stakic he went through a very large number of documents. He will not be doing that this time because, as I say, I'll be relying on Your Honours to read the transcript together with the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we also need time to read these documents because I personally haven't even started looking at them. And that's -- that's the absolute truth. I mean my intention -- the advantage I have over Mr. Ackerman is that I don't need to prepare a cross-examination. So I can read them keeping pace with --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, effectively he's repeated the same thing over and over again. Your Honour really only needs to read, Mr. Ackerman may want to pick him up on some odd inconsistencies but the Stakic testimony covers everything that he ever dealt with and all he does in -- he repeats in Keraterm he was only brought for cross-examination in Keraterm, he just repeats effectively the Tadic. Mr. Ackerman I perfectly understand has to go through it because if he wants to cross-examine inconsistencies but for Your Honours purposes I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For our purposes exactly, I mean, our purposes -- if I were Defence counsel I would go through every single line and every single word there is in all of those documents to see whether I could take advantage of any of them but as a Judge, I can make my selection. I mean that's -- because after all --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When I --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And I can read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour can I put it this way? I am trying to move this case along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I am too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: One of the reasons we are trying to move this case along is Mr. Brdjanin has been in custody for a long time. If Your Honours -- if Mr. Ackerman on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin wants to put this case back because he says that he has difficulties, I would suggest one of the ways of alleviating those difficulties is for example his legal assistants does I know read English, and may be able it to do some of the work. His co-counsel doesn't, which is a drawback. We will be providing in any event the tapes of the -- but if Your Honours want this gap then I've said everything I need to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It takes time. Even listening to tapes if you're going to provide tapes, it takes time. My preference is to start on the 21st. That's definitely my preference. If Mr. Ackerman confirms again that he feels he will not be in a position to do his -- fulfil his responsibilities towards his client, adequately, if we did that, we started on the 21st, I have no option but to take it into consideration because I don't -- see -- in what he's stated so far, any capricious or any light-hearted reason for his submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'll just tell you and my colleagues here will confirm it if I need, when I learned from Ms. Korner yesterday that she planned to finish what I think was early with Kljuc, because she told us earlier this week that by the end of the month she would be finished with it. I went into panic. I mean, I was in a complete panic mode. I was running around, screaming, and throwing things because I just knew I couldn't possibly get ready for the 21st to start the Prijedor phase and I laid awake last night worrying about it, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, so let's settle it now. We will not be sitting on the 21st, 22nd, and 23rd of October. And a new scheduling order will be issued. But we'll be sitting on November 20, 21, and 22, with this understanding. On the 22nd, on my -- if we retain salle d'audience numero III, number III, there is court maintenance so please try to find another courtroom for the day. Maybe court maintenance will be ready in the morning and we can sit in the afternoon. They take a whole day for court maintenance?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have to contract with the external contractors to come in and do this maintenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've asked how many times about this sitting or not sitting all day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stakic will start again on when?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Scheduling order at the moment is for the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Scheduling order.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dependant on a new Judge being able to read her way through 80 days of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But just make a note that I would like to sit, to find a courtroom. Maybe they don't start on the 18th, in which case we will take their place. All right? And there is an appeals hearing in the afternoon of November 22nd as well. So we keep an eye on that. Any way, we will try and do our best but.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course the other -- I know that your two colleagues are involved in another case where there is a judgement expected in the not-too-distant future. I don't know whether there is a date for that as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not that I know of. I haven't been informed any way. Okay. We'll meet again on Monday. Have a nice weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of October, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
